headline: Every metal on Earth was forged in dying stars or cosmic collisions billions of years ago
universal_truth: We are literally made of stardust—connected to the cosmos at the atomic level
fun_facts: All gold on Earth was created by neutron star collisions billions of years ago
Iron is created in the final moments of massive stars before they explode as supernovas
The iron in your blood and the iron in Earth's core came from the same stellar processes
discussion_questions: How does knowing you're made of stardust change how you see yourself?
Why did it take dying stars to create the elements we need for life?
What does our cosmic origin say about our connection to the universe?

hook.script: The iron in your blood. The copper in your wires. The gold in your jewelry. None of it came from Earth. Every metal atom on our planet was forged in the heart of a dying star or the collision of neutron stars—billions of years before Earth existed.

cliff.script: The early universe contained only hydrogen and helium—no metals, no Earth, no possibility of life as we know it. How did these heavy elements come to exist? What cosmic forge created the ingredients for planets and people?

options.text: Nuclear fusion in stars and explosions of supernovas scattered metals across space
options.response: Yes. Stars fuse light elements into heavier ones; when they die, they scatter these elements into space.

options.text: Chemical reactions in early nebulas combined lighter elements
options.response: Chemistry rearranges atoms, but creating new elements requires nuclear fusion...

fact1.title: Stellar Forges
fact1.script: Stars are fusion reactors—crushing hydrogen into helium, then into carbon, oxygen, and heavier elements. But fusion stops at iron. Creating heavier elements requires the violence of a supernova—the explosive death of a massive star.

fact2.title: Gold From Collisions
fact2.script: Gold, platinum, and other heavy elements require even more extreme conditions—neutron star collisions. Two dead stars spiraling together and smashing create these precious metals. Every gold atom on Earth witnessed cosmic violence we can barely imagine.

fact3.title: Stardust in Your Blood
fact3.script: The iron that makes your blood red was forged in a star that died before our sun was born. The calcium in your bones, the oxygen you breathe—all created in stellar cores. You are literally made of stardust, assembled by billions of years of cosmic recycling.

wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: You are the universe experiencing itself. The atoms in your body traveled through stars and space to become you. We're not separate from the cosmos—we're made of it. That's not poetry; it's physics.

outro.script: That's Day 70—ten weeks of learning! Tomorrow, we'll discover what's in the air you breathe. Until then, remember: every atom in you has a story measured in billions of years.

growTrack.title: Cosmic Connection - Feel Your Stardust
growTrack.learning_objective: Experience visceral connection to cosmic origins
growTrack.activity: Look at your hands. The atoms in them were forged in stars that died before our sun was born. Spend one minute feeling this cosmic connection—you are the universe organized into a person, briefly. What does this awareness change?
